entries.title: Standalone Planning Docs
entries.description: Recovered and established standalone DEV-PATH.md/DEV-PLAN.md for the Cockpit repo, separate from eco's CK.00/CK.01/CK.02 governance.

entries.title: Audit Current eco Cockpit Files Against CK.01/CK.02
entries.description: Correction-pass audit of eco's embedded Cockpit implementation against the CK.01/CK.02 specs, ahead of extraction planning.

entries.title: Extraction Shape Decision
entries.description: Decided Cockpit's extraction shape: Python package boundary as the public API, with VS Code bridge and future standalone shell as adapters on top of it.

entries.title: Public API Surface
entries.description: Defined Cockpit's public consumer API as the Phase 1 Python package adapter boundary; VS Code and future standalone shells are hosts over that same API.

entries.title: Packaging Checklist (Primary)
entries.description: Packaging checklist for Track B B.2-02: Python package install/bridge smoke commands, VS Code host build, extension dev-host visual smoke, bridge resolution order, VSIX release exclusions.

entries.title: VS Code Host-to-Python Adapter Bridge
entries.description: VS Code host consumes the Phase 1 Python package adapter boundary through a read-only JSON bridge (cockpit.host_bridge): health, get_state, list_records, get_record.

entries.title: Bridge Packaging and Diagnostics Hardening
entries.description: Explicit bridge resolution order (packageRoot setting, sibling checkout, active Python environment) and 'eco: Cockpit Bridge Health' diagnostic command. VSIX must not bundle private planning/bootstrap docs.

entries.title: Phase 1 Package Install Automation
entries.description: cockpit.install_phase1 and the cockpit-install-phase1 console entrypoint: editable package install, test verification, read-only bridge health smoke against a selected eco workspace.

entries.title: Explicit Apply for Install Automation
entries.description: install_phase1 follows explicit-apply: preview by default, --apply required to mutate the active Python environment. Aligns with GC zero-trust expectations.

entries.title: Screenshot/Demo Flow
entries.description: Demo flow using the VS Code Extension Development Host against C:\dev\eco, positioning Cockpit as a bridge-backed operator surface: setup commands, visible signals, screenshot sequence, claims boundaries.

entries.title: Marlin Governance Panel (Primary)
entries.description: First concrete use of Cockpit's universal UI host role: surfaces Marlin-DXP's install, audit validate, and status operations inside Cockpit as a governance panel, removing the need for a standalone Marlin GUI.

entries.title: Marlin Panel Install-Readiness Slice
entries.description: First Marlin governance panel slice: read-only install-readiness record type on the Marlin adapter and host bridge, with an explicit apply command as an approval artifact. Bridge rejects apply attempts through the read-only query.

entries.title: Cockpit UI Extraction (Primary)
entries.description: Extract Cockpit's webview UI (HTML/CSS/JS) out of eco-vscode and eco/surfaces/vscode/eco-vs into a host-agnostic bundle owned by cockpit/, so Cockpit ships its own installable UI that any host (VS Code, future Electron, browser) can mount via a thin loader against the existing Python bridge.

entries.title: Feature-Parity Audit - eco-vs vs Extracted Bundle
entries.description: Audit comparing the older embedded eco-vs Cockpit implementation against the extracted host-agnostic Cockpit bundle and current eco-vscode host loader, classifying parity gaps and the next compound restoration PASS.

entries.title: UI-Only Operator Parity Port
entries.description: Retroactive registration: ports the seven UI-only parity surfaces (run list/detail/copy/rerun, escalation approve/deny, artifact list/open, PASS run launcher, policy viewer/editor) into the extracted cockpit/web bundle against existing adapter calls, per the CKP.08.04 audit's Finding 3. Implemented and closed under the informal, unregistered name CKP.08.04a before this correction - DEV-ACCORD.02 does not permit letter-suffixed sub-passes (three-level CLUSTER.NN.NN.letter form); this is a sibling sub-pass of CKP.08.04 under CKP.08.00, not a child of CKP.08.04.

entries.title: Artifact Trash/Restore Backend Contract
entries.description: Adds delete_record/restore_record to the CockpitAdapter ABC and implements soft-delete (move to .eco/.trash/artifacts) plus restore for EcoAdapter, with path-containment checks matching the proven eco-vs deleteArtifact/restoreArtifact semantics. Wired into host_bridge.py as delete_record/restore_record operations. Closes the first of the two real backend gaps identified in the CKP.08.04 audit (governance diagnostics and editor-plane sync remain open). Cited as CKP.08.04b before this correction, per the same DEV-ACCORD.02 letter-suffix issue as CKP.08.05.

entries.title: Governance Diagnostics Record Type
entries.description: Adds a governance record type to CockpitAdapter/EcoAdapter, merging governance-diagnostics.json, project.yaml's governance_mode, and health-report.json's overall_score into one record - the three sources the old eco-vs Governance tab read directly. Flows through the existing generic list_records/get_record dispatch (no host_bridge.py changes needed). Relayed through cockpitApi.ts/webviewHost.ts and rendered as a Governance tab in the extracted bundle. Closes the second of the two real backend gaps identified in the CKP.08.04 audit.

entries.title: Editor-Plane Sync via Polling
entries.description: Live active-PASS/run-state/governance-state status bar in the extracted bundle dashboard, kept current by the VS Code host loader polling getState()/diagnostics on an interval while the panel is visible and pushing only on change - deliberately not the old eco-vs push-on-file-change model, decided as a portfolio-owner architecture call to fit the existing request/response bridge contract without new adapter or host-side watcher plumbing.

entries.title: PASS-ID Citation Gate Wiring
entries.description: Wires governance-commons/gc-audit/tools/validate-pass-citations.ps1 into this repo's git hooks (pre-commit + commit-msg, via .pre-commit-config.yaml) for the first time - this repo had no git hooks at all before this. Companion fix in governance-commons widened the validator's heading regex to recognize this repo's leading-alias '## CKP.NN Closure' convention. Found via a portfolio-wide dirty/sync scan during the CKP.08.06 PLAY. Registered after the fact - cited informally in commit messages and DEV-PATH.md before this registration, using Pass-ID: standalone in the actual commit trailers rather than a false PASS-ID claim.

entries.title: eco-vs Cockpit Panel Superseded
entries.description: Decision: eco/surfaces/vscode/eco-vs's Cockpit panel is superseded by the extracted cockpit/web bundle plus eco-vscode host loader, now that all 5 CK.01 required surfaces and eco-vs's two extras (Governance, editor-plane sync) are covered - see CKP.08.05 through CKP.08.08. Verified by tsc/build/pytest plus a manual Extension Development Host smoke test against C:\dev\eco (portfolio owner, 2026-07-02): all tabs render, no console errors, Governance tab degrades gracefully. Not exhaustively verified: artifact delete/undo round-trip and the Governance tab's non-empty-data path were not explicitly exercised live - recorded as a known residual gap, not a blocker. Does not affect eco-vs's HELM or PASS surfaces, which remain active and out of scope.

entries.title: v1.0 Scoping and Durable Cockpit/Marlin Boundary (Primary)
entries.description: Breaks eco-ui-spec's five locked v1.0 items into real, estimable PASSes (mode switching, diagnostics dashboard, Quick-Bar, environment setup wizard, environment emergence UI); corrects a discrepancy between that locked spec and cockpit's own Product Ladder table. Records the durable Cockpit/Marlin boundary the portfolio owner set after flagging that planning-doc language had drifted toward framing Cockpit as Marlin's UI: Cockpit is the universal UI/UX host (identity, not narrowed to any one backend); Marlin owns install/scaffold/audit/package/governance-setup logic; adapters own the typed contract between them. Verified the actual MarlinAdapter/install_phase1.py code already respects this boundary - the drift was in planning-doc language, not the implementation. Sets Marlin's environment-setup UI as the priority build target inside Cockpit's universal scope, not a narrowing of that scope.

entries.title: Environment Setup Wizard Shell
entries.description: Generic wizard shell in the extracted bundle: step sequence, progress state (step indicator with active/complete states), and Back/Next navigation. Steps are pluggable (id, title, render, isComplete) so future provider setup flows can register without changing the shell. CKP.07's Marlin install-readiness preview is wired in as the one real step today - same read-only/preview data as the dashboard's existing Marlin panel, rendered independently for the wizard so the dashboard panel is unchanged. Built per the CKP.09.00 durable boundary: this is Marlin's environment-setup UI hosted as a provider surface inside Cockpit's universal wizard shell, not a narrowing of Cockpit to Marlin.

entries.title: Marlin Provider Real Install and Niji Provider
entries.description: Adds the first real provider action to the generic environment setup wizard: Marlin package search and explicit-confirm install rendered in Cockpit while Marlin remains the package/install authority and eco-vscode owns host subprocess execution. Adds a read-only Niji provider adapter/panel for health, schemes, and sample palette preview. Confirms the CKP.09.00 boundary: Universal Cockpit hosts provider workflows; it does not absorb Marlin or Niji domain authority.

entries.title: Headless DOM Smoke Tests for the Extracted Web Bundle
entries.description: Adds pytest-playwright headless-Chromium smoke tests (src/cockpit/tests/test_web_bundle_smoke.py) loading web/cockpit.html + cockpit.js + cockpit.css with the host-template placeholders substituted the same way webviewHost.ts does. Verifies the bundle renders with zero console errors and posts the correct eco.cockpit.* message for each UI-only operator-parity action from CKP.08.04a. Does not re-test eco-vscode snapshot assembly or adapter/backend logic. pytest-playwright declared in this repo's own pyproject.toml [test] extra, not a sibling repo's shared venv, per the portfolio-wide modularity/portability standard.

entries.title: Lasso Workspace and Marlin Workspace Explorer Panels
entries.description: Adds two new universal-host provider surfaces to the extracted bundle. Lasso Workspace is a multi-lane prompt-compose panel (Codex/Claude/Reviewer lanes with per-lane include toggles, a shared prompt input, and a client-side merge into a composed-output textarea) reflecting the portfolio's existing 3-agent workflow, with no backend adapter of its own - browser-local only. Marlin Workspace Explorer adds a read-only workspace-tree/repo-status surface: MarlinAdapter gains `workspace-tree` and `repo-status` record types, a depth/item-bounded directory walk with a skip-list for noise directories (.git, node_modules, .venv, build caches, etc.), path-containment enforcement via `_resolve_contained_path` (same pattern as the CKP.08.06 artifact trash/restore contract, refusing to resolve outside the workspace root or through UNC paths), and a `git status --porcelain=v1 --branch` shell-out per repo for branch/dirty detection. Registered retroactively: the implementing commit (9260f15) used `Change-Level: DRIVE` with `Dev-Docs: not-needed`, which is non-conformant with DEV-ACCORD.06 (DRIVE requires `Dev-Docs: updated`) - this registration plus the DEV-PATH/DEV-PLAN closure entries is that correction.

entries.title: Workspace Explorer Repo Status UI, Connection Badge, and Responsive Shell Layout
entries.description: Follow-up UI pass on CKP.10.00's Marlin Workspace Explorer. Renders the `repo-status` records the backend already exposed but the bundle did not yet display: a repository card grid (name, path, git branch/dirty state, registry match) under the workspace tree/inspector. Adds a topbar connection badge (`Host connected` vs `Preview mode`, driven by whether a real Cockpit host answered) so the operator can tell live data from static preview data at a glance. Adds a two-tier nav grouping (Operate / Providers labels above the tab list) and a wide-viewport (>=1040px) responsive shell layout that moves the tab list into a sticky left rail instead of a horizontal bar. Also enriches the bundle's static preview-mode fixture data (fake runs, escalations, artifacts, policies, install-readiness, workspace tree, repo statuses) so preview mode exercises the same render paths as a live host instead of showing empty states.

entries.title: Mode Switching (HELM) - Host-Agnostic Adapter Read/Write
entries.description: Implements the v1.0 ladder's 'mode switching' item from docs/specifications/CKP.v1.0-scoping.md, which identified real prior art (HELM's 5-mode system, eco/passes/helm/HELM.00-02.md) rather than new invented scope. Per the CKP.03 three-phase architecture decision (Python package is host-agnostic; VS Code and any future standalone shell are adapters on top of it, not separate APIs), the entire feature - both reading current mode/history and writing a mode change - lives in EcoAdapter (new 'mode' record type; list_records/get_record read <workspace_root>/.eco/helm/mode_history.json with the same graceful-degradation pattern as CKP.08.07's governance record; submit('mode', {mode}) appends a HelmModeChange-shaped entry, pure file I/O, no subprocess or VS Code API). Explicitly does not port eco-vs's helm.ts/helm-session.ts implementation into eco-vscode and does not touch eco-vs or the eco repo at all - an earlier draft of this PASS proposed exactly that porting approach and was corrected mid-session after the portfolio owner objected that it would make the feature itself VS-Code-dependent, contradicting CKP.03. eco-vscode's role is limited to the same thin, generic message-relay every other write action (approve escalation, save policy, delete artifact) already requires. Bundle UI adds an 'Operator Mode' tile to the dashboard's editor-plane-sync status bar and a HELM Mode section (selector, Activate button, change history) to the Governance tab.

entries.title: Standalone Web Host - CKP.03 Phase 3 Implemented
entries.description: Implements CKP.03.00's reserved-but-unbuilt third packaging form: 'Universal standalone shell: Electron or web app host; no VS Code dependency; same adapter API as phases 1 and 2.' New host-web/ directory: a plain Express server serving the unmodified web/cockpit.{html,css,js} bundle and relaying eco.cockpit.* messages to python -m cockpit.host_bridge over HTTP instead of VS Code's postMessage channel, proving docs/specifications/CKP.08-host-loader-contract.md's host-agnostic bundle contract for real - that doc already speced this exact 'small local HTTP shim' case before any code existed. Deployment model: locally-run tool only (npm start, point at your own workspace) - a public multi-tenant hosted version is named Phase 4 in DEV-PATH.md, planned and deliberately deferred, not scoped here. Two real gaps found during build: the bundle's static CSP has no connect-src (blocks fetch(), fixed server-side with a permissive CSP substitution); marlin search's query is a positional CLI arg with no stdin alternative (unlike claude/codex), so the PATH-based .cmd fallback is refused outright rather than accepting a shell-injection risk - only the safe sibling-checkout path (real .exe, no shell) is supported. Three actions with no clean web equivalent (clipboard copy, VS Code editor open, native install-confirm dialog) are downgraded to honest alternatives instead of faked.

entries.title: Phase 4 Multi-Tenant Hosting Design
entries.description: Design-only pass (no implementation) for DEV-PATH.md's Phase 4 - a genuinely public, multi-tenant hosted Cockpit deferred by CKP.11.00/Phase 16 as its own security-critical planning pass. Portfolio-wide search found no existing auth, multi-tenancy, or subprocess-sandboxing precedent anywhere in c:\dev. Recommends a thin control plane (new host-cloud/ directory, colocated in this repo) in front of unmodified, one-per-tenant Phase 3 host-web instances running in containers, reusing Phase 16's own stated design principle. Documents: control-plane vs per-tenant-container responsibilities; an explicitly undecided auth-model tradeoff (GitHub OAuth vs email magic link); session handling that derives workspaceRoot only from the authenticated tenant, never client input; subprocess sandboxing via the container boundary plus the existing stdin-not-argv precedent (marlinCli.js, lasso/spawnAgent.js); a path-containment gap (existing helpers are lexical-only and don't follow symlinks/junctions, must resolve via fs.realpath/Path.resolve(strict=True) before the containment check); capability boundaries per action class (read-only panels vs mutating actions) in addition to tenancy boundaries; and abuse/resource limits. Also fixed, as a separate small patch surfaced during this design review (Phase 3 hardening, not part of the Phase 4 design itself): host-web/index.js defaulted to binding all network interfaces with zero auth - now defaults to 127.0.0.1, overridable via COCKPIT_HOST.

entries.title: Auth Model Decision + Tenant-Registry Skeleton
entries.description: Closes CKP.12.00's open auth-model decision (GitHub OAuth, per that doc's recommendation) and builds the first real implementation slice of the Phase 4 control plane: new host-cloud/ directory (colocated in this repo, sibling to host-web/), containing a JSON-file-backed tenant registry (tenantRegistry.js), a stateless HMAC-SHA256-signed session token (session.js, a small self-written signer rather than a JWT dependency, for a fixed tiny claim set), a GitHub OAuth login/callback flow (githubAuth.js), and one proof endpoint (POST /api/whoami) demonstrating the core design invariant end-to-end: workspaceRoot is resolved only from the server-owned tenant record looked up by the session token's tenantId claim, never from request body/query/headers - proven by a dedicated regression test in host-cloud/tests/server.test.js that sends a forged workspaceRoot and tenantId in the body and asserts the response still reflects the authenticated caller's own record. Also closes the symlink/junction containment gap CKP.12.00 flagged: host-cloud/pathContainment.js adds resolveContainedPathStrict, resolving through fs.realpathSync before the containment comparison, unlike host-web/pathContainment.js's lexical-only check; a real symlink-escape test exists and self-skips (not silently passes) in environments where symlink creation needs elevated privileges. No container orchestration, rate limiting/quotas/idle-teardown, capability-scoped tokens, or actual proxying to a tenant's host-web instance were built in this pass - all named as future scope. host-web and the Python cockpit package are unchanged.

entries.title: Process Orchestration, Rate/Quota Limits, Capability Tokens, Real Proxying
entries.description: Compound PASS closing all four items CKP.13.00 named as future scope, done together at the portfolio owner's request. Docker was attempted for real first (Docker Desktop launch on this ARM64/Windows-build-26200 machine) and failed with WSL_E_WSL_MOUNT_NOT_SUPPORTED (wsl.exe --mount requires build 27653+) - confirmed as a platform-version gap, not sign-in/config; CKP.12.00's container design is unaffected and remains the target once a compatible Docker host exists. Built instead: processManager.js spawns one real, unmodified host-web (CKP.11.00) child process per tenant - real OS-process isolation, container-manager-shaped interface (ensureRunning/stop/sweepIdle/touch) for a later Docker swap-in, readiness detected via host-web's own 'listening on' stdout line. rateLimiter.js (per-tenant token bucket). quota.js (best-effort application-level disk usage check, honestly documented as not real enforcement - true quotas need filesystem/container-runtime support this stand-in lacks). session.js gained a capabilities claim (['read','write'] default, or a narrower ['read']-only token); capabilities.js maps every eco.cockpit.* type from host-web/actions.js's dispatch switch to read or write (fails closed to write for unrecognized types) and enforces it independently of tenancy via requireCapability. proxy.js + server.js's real POST /api/bridge chain (requireSession -> requireRateLimit -> requireCapability -> quota check -> processManager.ensureRunning -> proxy.forward), relaying the tenant's real host-web response unchanged per CKP.08-host-loader-contract.md. A real bug was caught only by the real (non-mocked) end-to-end test built for this pass: requireSession built req.tenant.workspaceRoot but processManager.ensureRunning originally read tenant.workspacePath - a property-name mismatch that would have silently given every tenant the control plane's own cwd instead of its isolated workspace; fixed by aligning processManager.js to tenant.workspaceRoot. Not built: real container orchestration (blocked on this machine's platform), an endpoint to issue narrower read-only tokens, true filesystem quota enforcement.

entries.title: Secure-Cookie Enforcement
entries.description: Fixes a real gap found by a security review of CKP.12.00-14.00's host-cloud/ code: server.js's serializeCookie never set the Secure attribute on the oauth_state or cockpit_session cookies. Since cockpit_session is the sole bearer credential for a control plane explicitly built for public multi-tenant hosting, and host-cloud defaults to binding 0.0.0.0 with no TLS of its own (TLS/reverse-proxy setup is deferred ops scope per CKP.12.00), this was a concrete session-hijacking vector via network interception in the PASS's own shipped default configuration, not a theoretical hardening gap. Fixed: serializeCookie takes a secure option (default true); index.js's new resolveRuntimeSecurity() fails closed - refuses to start on a non-loopback bind unless COCKPIT_CLOUD_TLS_TERMINATED=1 (real HTTPS termination, cookies get Secure) or an explicit COCKPIT_CLOUD_ALLOW_INSECURE_HTTP=1 opt-out (local/dev-only, cookies drop Secure too since a Secure cookie over plain HTTP is simply never sent by the browser). Loopback binding (127.0.0.1/localhost/::1) is allowed without either flag, matching host-web's own local-dev posture.

entries.title: Read-Only Token Issuance Endpoint
entries.description: Closes CKP.14.00's named gap: capability-scoped tokens existed but there was no way to actually issue a narrower one. POST /api/tokens/readonly (server.js) lets any authenticated tenant mint a token scoped to exactly ['read'], regardless of the caller's own capabilities - never an escalation, since the issued token's capability set is fixed rather than inherited or widened. ttlSeconds is accepted and clamped to [60, 86400] (1 minute to 24 hours), defaulting to 1 hour, so a caller cannot mint an effectively-permanent token via an absurd TTL. A necessary companion change: requireSession only read the cockpit_session cookie, so a token minted here would have had no way to actually be used by a non-browser caller (no cookie jar) - requireSession now also accepts Authorization: Bearer <token> as a fallback after the cookie, same session.verify() call, no new trust boundary.

entries.title: Diagnostics Dashboard Expansion
entries.description: Builds the v1.0 ladder's Diagnostics panel item (CKP.v1.0-scoping.md), whose locked spec (eco/docs/specifications/cockpit-ui-spec.md) requires 'unified status for runtime health, integrations, environment checks, and agent pipelines' - three categories the scoping doc admitted had no identified data source. Research first (not invented scope): integrations = cheap, already existed (EcoAdapter/MarlinAdapter/NijiAdapter health() all already return a uniform shape; only marlin('health') was missing from the snapshot call - added). Environment checks = genuinely new, no existing source anywhere in the portfolio - portfolio owner decided the scope: a minimal toolchain check (Python interpreter/version + cockpit package importable, Node version), new SystemAdapter (backend_id 'system', not workspace-scoped, registered in host_bridge.py's _build_adapter). Agent pipelines = medium, raw data existed in PLAY.jsonl (a per-repo dev-process ledger, this portfolio's own governance convention) but nothing aggregated it - new EcoAdapter record type 'agent-pipeline' reads <workspace_root>/PLAY.jsonl (graceful degradation if absent, matching every other _read_* method's pattern) and aggregates by declared_by. Wired into both host-web (snapshotBuilder.js) and eco-vscode (cockpitApi.ts's new createPythonSystemCockpitApi, webviewHost.ts's buildCockpitSnapshot/loadMarlinInstallReadiness) so both hosts stay in sync per CKP.08's contract, and into the bundle (web/cockpit.html/js) as a new Diagnostics tab: Integrations status grid, Environment status grid, Agent Pipelines table. Static preview-mode fixture data enriched to match.
